reader.title: Killing of Dr. Eady and capture of Baggott near Durango
bases: The detailed wires describe a murder, an arrest by policemen, an escape and a recapture by a posse after a fight in which a policeman was killed, with the captive expected to 'be shot' (A2, A6, A14); only a brief digest calls his death a lynching (A12).

A digest line says Baggott 'was lynched on the 4th' (A12), and one wire version says he 'was shot early to-day' (A3), but most copies of the same wire say only that he 'will be shot' after capture by policemen and a posse (A2, A6, A10), and none names a mob or says who would shoot him. The coverage does not establish that he was killed, or that a group acting outside the law killed him.

The digest reports a lynching on January 4 (A12, A13, A17), while the fuller Nogales wire, in most copies, reports a capture by police and an expected shooting (A2, A4, A6, A14), and one copy reports the shooting as done (A3).

summary.text: The killing of Dr. Eady and capture of Baggott near Durango took place in early January 1888, when an American named Baggott was accused of shooting Eady, an Englishman, over a disputed ranch, then escaped arrest and was recaptured by a posse.
Wire reports from Nogales said the captured man would be shot, one copy said he had been shot, and a weekly news digest said he 'was lynched on the 4th'.
No report describes a mob, and papers disagreed over whether the event took place in Arizona or Mexico.
According to the Nogales dispatches, Eady had bought a ranch near Baggott's that Baggott also claimed.
When Eady visited the place, Baggott demanded the deed, and on Eady's refusal shot him several times, one shot breaking his spine.
The wire described Eady as 'a man of considerable wealth' who was well known in the United States.
Baggott went to Durango, where he was arrested.
Allowed to tend his horse, he mounted, fired at the policemen and escaped to the mountains.
A posse followed and fought him in a cave; one policeman was killed and others were wounded.
Baggott was captured, in the wire's words, 'after being nearly beaten to death'.
What happened next is reported differently.
Most copies of the dispatch said that 'the murderer will be shot early to day' or simply 'will be shot', without saying by whom.
The Los Angeles Daily Herald's copy of the same dispatch ended instead that 'the murderer was shot early to-day', under a headline counting three deaths.
A San Francisco dispatch of January 7, reprinted in Arizona, still said he 'will be shot at an early day'.
No report of Baggott's death beyond these lines, or of an inquest or trial, appears in the coverage.

The story spread as a single Nogales telegram, printed on January 5 and 6 in papers from Omaha and Salt Lake City to Washington, Richmond, Savannah and New York, and later in Atlanta, Kansas and Arizona weeklies.

Headlines stressed the crime and the nationalities involved: 'Brutal Murder in Arizona' in the Omaha Daily Bee, 'An Englishman Brutally Murdered by an American' in the Savannah Morning News, and 'Successful Chase After a Murderer' in the New-York Tribune.
Every version called Baggott 'the murderer' before any trial.
The word 'lynched' appeared only in a syndicated weekly digest run by Minnesota and other country papers from January 11 to 14, which gave the place as 'Durango, A. T.'.
Others located the event differently: the Washington Evening Star headed its item 'Murder by an American in Mexico', and the Waterbury Evening Democrat placed the ranch 'near Durango, Mexico'.
The Hawaiian Gazette's summary, by contrast, put the murder 'in Arizona'.
The digest's report of a lynching on January 4 conflicts with the fuller telegram, which in most copies reported only that Baggott was in the hands of the police posse and would be shot.
The Salt Lake Herald and Los Angeles Daily Herald printed the same January 4 dispatch word for word except for its final verb, 'will be shot' against 'was shot', so one paper altered it.

accounts.label: Nogales wire (most copies)
accounts.gist: Baggott killed Eady, was arrested at Durango, escaped, killed a policeman in a fight with a posse and was captured; he 'will be shot'.

accounts.label: Nogales wire (Los Angeles copy)
accounts.gist: Same account, but ending that the murderer 'was shot early to-day', under a headline counting three deaths.

accounts.label: Weekly news digest
accounts.gist: A one-line item that 'a murderer named Baggott was lynched on the 4th near Durango, A. T.', with no detail.

framing.detail: Papers ran the Nogales wire under headlines such as 'Brutal Murder in Arizona', 'An Englishman Brutally Murdered by an American' and 'Successful Chase After a Murderer', calling Baggott 'the murderer' throughout.
The weekly digest reported the lynching in one line among unrelated items, without comment.

versions.value: captured and 'will be shot' (early that day / at an early day)

conflicts.note: The Los Angeles copy and the Salt Lake copy carry the same Nogales, January 4 wire with the same wording except the final verb, so one of them altered it; the digest's 'lynched' is a later one-line summary and gives no source.
The wires themselves say only 'near Durango City' and 'Durango', datelined Nogales; papers' headlines and summaries placed it in different countries.

record_check.dossier: Insufficient: the lynching claim rests on a one-line digest; the detailed wires describe capture by police and a posse and an expected shooting, with no mob named.
Uncertain: the wires were datelined Nogales, Arizona, but say only 'near Durango City'; two papers placed it in Mexico, others in Arizona.
Accused of shooting Dr. Eady, an Englishman, over a disputed ranch deed, and of killing a policeman in the fight at his recapture.
Policemen and a posse captured him; who was to shoot him, or did, is not stated.
Recaptured by a posse after escaping from arrest; no report says he was taken from officers.

record_check.record: A murderer named Baggott was lynched on January 4 near Durango, A. T. The paper gives no further detail on the mob or the circumstances.
record_check.dossier: Fuller wires report the murder of Dr. Eady, Baggott's arrest, escape and recapture, and an expected or completed shooting; only the digest says 'lynched'.

info: Dispatches dated January 4 and 5, 1888, reported the murder, escape and recapture; the digest dates the lynching to January 4
Near 'Durango City' / Durango; the wires were datelined Nogales, Arizona
Baggott (also Baggot, Baggett), described as 'an American'; his murder victim was Dr. Eady (also 'Brady', 'Eardy'), 'an Englishman'
Accused of shooting Dr. Eady in a dispute over a ranch both claimed, after Eady refused to give up the deed
Baggott was arrested by policemen and recaptured by a posse; no mob is named in the detailed wires; the digest names no actor
Contested: 'will be shot early to day' / 'will be shot' vs. 'was shot early to-day' vs. 'was lynched on the 4th'
